with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`

abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,

normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

## Survey of this case, computed by code

A starting point, not the answer: it ranks nothing out. Check what it shows, and look beyond it.

content.text: I'll start by checking which spans in `search` slowed down, since its own time grew while its callees' latencies stayed flat.

input.query: SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration, 0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY p95_ms DESC LIMIT 30

content.text: The slowdown sits in `search.Search/Nearby` and its `rate.Rate/GetRates` child, but the survey shows `rate` itself as normal. I'll look at a slow trace's full span tree to see where the time goes.

input.query: WITH slow AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='search.Search/Nearby' AND duration>1e9 LIMIT 1) SELECT t.trace_id, t.service_name, t.span_name, t.parent_span_id, t.span_id, t.start_time, t.duration/1e6 ms, t.attr_status_code FROM abnormal_traces t JOIN slow USING(trace_id) ORDER BY start_time
SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration, 0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 30

WITH slow AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='search.Search/Nearby' AND duration>1e9 LIMIT 1) SELECT t.service_name, t.span_name, t.parent_span_id, t.span_id, t."timestamp", t.duration/1e6 ms, t.attr_status_code FROM abnormal_traces t JOIN slow USING(trace_id) ORDER BY "timestamp"
SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration, 0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 30

content.text: The `rate` service's own spans are fast (about 1 ms), while `search` sees its `rate.Rate/GetRates` call take 2.7 s. That gap suggests the time is spent between the two services rather than inside `rate`. I'll pull one slow trace's full tree to confirm.

input.query: WITH slow AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND service_name='search' AND duration>1e9 LIMIT 1) SELECT t.service_name, t.span_name, t.parent_span_id, t.span_id, t.duration/1e6 ms, t.attr_status_code, t.attr_peer_address FROM abnormal_traces t JOIN slow USING(trace_id)
SELECT 'abn' p, metric_name, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', metric_name, count(*) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: The output was too broad. I'll narrow to the `rate`, `search` and `reservation` services and check restarts, uptime and CPU across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, avg(value) v, min(value) mn, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('rate','search','reservation') AND metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','container.cpu.usage') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), avg(value), min(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('rate','search','reservation') AND metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','container.cpu.usage') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Reservation's container CPU jumped from about 0.006 to about 3.3 cores, a clear saturation signal. Next I'll check the slow search→rate trace tree with explicit columns, and the logs.

input.query: WITH slow AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND service_name='search' AND duration>1e9 LIMIT 1) SELECT t.service_name, t.span_name, t.parent_span_id, t.span_id, t.duration/1e6 AS ms, t.attr_status_code FROM abnormal_traces t JOIN slow USING(trace_id)

SELECT service_name, severity_text, body, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE severity_text IN ('ERROR','WARN','FATAL','error','warn') OR body ILIKE '%error%' OR body ILIKE '%timeout%' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 25

content.text: The search→rate client span runs 2.17 s while the `rate` server span takes 0.8 ms, so about 2.2 s is lost between the two. Now the logs.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 25

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, metric, count(*) n, avg(value) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','rate','search','frontend') AND metric LIKE '%cpu%' OR (service_name IN ('reservation','rate','search') AND metric LIKE 'jvm%') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3

content.text: Reservation's CPU saturation is real but its effect on users looks small (about 1 ms on its own spans). I'll list all metric names to see whether any network or connection metrics exist that could explain the search→rate gap.

input.query: SELECT 'sum' t, metric, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'g', metric, count(*) FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'h', metric, count(*) FROM abnormal_metrics_histogram GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2

content.text: There are pod-level network metrics (`k8s.pod.network.io` and `k8s.pod.network.errors`). I'll compare them for `search`, `rate` and `frontend` across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, count(*) n, avg(value) v, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io','k8s.pod.uptime') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, count(*), avg(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io','k8s.pod.uptime') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,4,1

content.text: Search and rate pods don't appear in the network metrics, so there's no per-connection evidence. Next I'll check how the search→rate delay evolves over the abnormal window, and compare with the reservation CPU timeline.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, floor(EXTRACT(epoch FROM "time") - (SELECT min(EXTRACT(epoch FROM "time")) FROM abnormal_traces))/30 AS bucket, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6 med_ms, min(duration)/1e6 min_ms, max(duration)/1e6 max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND service_name='search' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2

SELECT t.service_name, t.span_name, t.span_id, t.parent_span_id, t.duration/1e6 ms FROM abnormal_traces t WHERE trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND span_name='HTTP /hotels' AND duration < 50e6 LIMIT 1) ORDER BY t.service_name

content.text: The search→rate delay is steady across the whole window (about 1.6–2.8 s per call), not a transient. Next I'll check whether reservation's CPU saturation reaches frontend, by comparing its spans and its callers' spans across both periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6 med_ms, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, max(duration)/1e6 mx_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','frontend') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, span_name, count(*), approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6, max(duration)/1e6 FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','frontend') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,2,1

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, count(*) n, avg(value) v, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','rate','search') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.container.ready') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, count(*), avg(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','rate','search') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.container.ready') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,4,1
